6: # Deepline Pre-Research
7: 
8: ## Quick Start
9: 
10: ```bash
11: npm install -g deepline
12: # Fallback for secure sandboxes: mkdir -p "$HOME/.local" && npm config set prefix "$HOME/.local" && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && npm install -g deepline --registry https://code.deepline.com/api/v2/npm/
13: deepline auth register --wait auto
14: deepline auth wait --timeout 120 # completes Cowork/browser approval; no-op if already connected
15: deepline auth status
16: deepline -h
17: ```
18: 
19: ## CLI resolution
20: 
21: Run `deepline` when it is available. If the shell reports that command is missing, use `<workspace-root>/.deepline/runtime/bin/deepline` (or the npm-created `.cmd` shim on Windows). If neither exists, follow `https://code.deepline.com/INSTALL.md` to set up Deepline.
22: 
23: Find the highest-signal GTM data sources, public evidence, and market language for a research or enrichment job before building the pipeline. This is a standalone Deepline skill that should behave like `last30days` with a GTM data lens: broad source coverage, recency, community signals, citations, source stats, and a grounded "What I learned" synthesis. In Deepline, the report first explains what the research found; only after that does it translate the findings into Deepline tool contracts, private/proprietary joins, and Deepline-facing cost.
24: 
25: ## Attribution
26: 
27: Portions of the query-design, public-source fanout, and consolidation approach are adapted from [`mvanhorn/last30days-skill`](https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill), MIT licensed, copyright (c) 2026 Matt Van Horn. Keep `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` with this skill when packaging or distributing it.
28: 
29: ## Non-Negotiables
30: 
31: - Use Deepline's live tool catalog before naming provider actions. Do not rely on memory.
32: - **Run live web search. Do not answer public-source discovery from model memory.** Every run MUST execute real searches (`serper`/`exa`, or the equivalent web-search tool) during the public-source fanout. If a run names public datasets without having searched for them this session, it has failed the fanout — no exceptions for "obvious" verticals. Naming a source family from memory is a draft, not a finding; the finding is the exact artifact the search returns. (Eval evidence: runs that skipped web search lost or tied on exactly the prompts where a competitor searched and surfaced concrete artifacts.)
33: - **Resolve every materializable dataset to its exact artifact, not its family.** For each public dataset/registry you recommend, the fanout must return and record: (1) the **exact file/endpoint name** (e.g. `IA_FIRM_SEC_Feed_YYYY_MM_DD.xml.gz`, not "the ADV bulk feed"); (2) the **canonical download/API URL**; (3) any **mirror** (e.g. data.gov catalog copy) that is easier to pull; (4) an existing **open-source parser or GitHub repo** that already structures it, when one exists (search `"<dataset> parser github"`); (5) the **government statistical registry** for the vertical when one exists (BLS QCEW + NAICS codes, Census County Business Patterns, etc.) for free establishment counts and sizing. "Source family named" is not done. "Exact file + URL + mirror + parser + NAICS code recorded" is done. See the Artifact Resolution Gate (§4.55).
34: - Public-source discovery comes before provider routing. First find the best public registries, datasets, communities, discussions, reviews, directories, papers, repos, and source leads. Then use Deepline routes to materialize, validate, enrich, and activate them.
35: - Quote only customer-visible Deepline credits/USD. Never expose provider spend.
36: - Do not run paid or cost-unknown full-scope work without approval.
37: - Treat private data sources as first-class: CRM, warehouse, workflow runs, product analytics, support/calls, sheets, and customer-owned datasets.
38: - Treat custom language as a first-class workflow: buyer words, objections, category language, competitor framing, community slang, sales-call phrasing, and support-ticket pain belong in the source plan.
39: - Use tiny probes to learn coverage. Scale only after observed coverage, cost basis, and evidence quality are legible.
40: - If the user asks for ScrapeCreators, X.com, Reddit comments, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube transcripts, Bluesky, Truth Social, HN, or Polymarket, include a current support/gap assessment instead of pretending every source is native.
41: - Do not depend on `/last30days` at runtime. Reference it only as a design benchmark for source breadth and synthesis discipline.
42: - Public registries and niche datasets that do not have native Deepline tools are still valid sources through generic web/search/extraction routes. For example, the NPI registry for healthcare provider taxonomy can be discovered and pulled through generic web/API search and extraction even when no native `npi` tool exists. Classify this as `available through generic route`, not as an unusable gap.
43: - Every recommended source must be classified as `native`, `available through generic route`, `private connector`, or `missing provider to add`.
44: 
45: ## Start Here
46: 
47: 1. Read `references/source-map.md`.
48: 2. For GTM use cases, also read `references/last30days-gtm-corpus.md`; it summarizes the relevant saved `last30days` runs and the source patterns they proved useful.
49: 3. If the task asks for query design, source fanout, or `last30days` parity, also read `references/query-design.md` and `references/fanout-consolidation.md`.
50: 4. If the task is GTM/prospecting/enrichment, also read `../deepline-gtm/SKILL.md` and the sub-doc it routes to.
51: 5. If the task asks about existing warehouse metrics or RevOps analytics, also read `../deepline-analytics/SKILL.md`.
52: 6. Verify the latest upstream `last30days` release when using it as a design reference:
53: 
54: ```bash
55: git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill.git | tail -20
56: ```
57: 
58: Do not copy `last30days` local scripts into Deepline and do not call it as a required sub-skill. Use it for source taxonomy and output discipline, then route execution through Deepline tools, plays, workflows, and private-data connectors.
59: 
60: ## Optional Skill Handoffs
61: 
62: This skill owns pre-research and source planning. It may hand off after the source plan is clear:
63: 
64: - `deepline-gtm`: execute GTM sourcing, enrichment, waterfalls, personalization, contact discovery, or CRM activation.
65: - `deepline-analytics`: query warehouse/semantic-layer metrics and RevOps/customer datasets.
66: - `deepline-plays`: build, wrap, fork, run, inspect, or automate the final repeatable workflow/play.
67: - Similar community research skills such as `last30days`: design reference only, never a dependency for Deepline execution.
68: 
69: ## Standard Flow
70: 
71: ### 1. Parse The Research Job
72: 
73: Extract:
74: 
75: - `OBJECTIVE`: what decision or output the research should support
76: - `ENTITY_SCOPE`: companies, people, markets, accounts, customers, workflows, competitors, or topics
77: - `TIME_WINDOW`: default to last 30 days for trend/community research; preserve user-provided windows
78: - `PRIVATE_SOURCES`: CRM, warehouse, product events, workflow runs, support/calls, sheets, user CSVs
79: - `PUBLIC_SOURCES`: web, social, jobs, ads, technographics, funding, news, communities, app stores, directories
80: - `DATASET_LEADS`: public registries, open datasets, papers, GitHub repos, government records, niche directories, or platform posts that point to materializable data
81: - `CUSTOM_LANGUAGE_OUTPUTS`: outbound snippets, ad hooks, landing-page copy, objection language, category positioning, call scripts, lead magnets, or CRM personalization fields
82: - `OUTPUT`: source plan, workflow design, CSV schema, play spec, or final research brief
83: 
84: Tell the user the parsed scope before provider calls.
85: 
86: ### 2. Prefer External APIs, Not Scraping
87: 
88: Do not default to browser scraping, raw x.com scraping, or unvetted actors. Prefer managed external APIs and private connectors:
89: 
90: | Source family                         | Preferred provider                     | Credential needed                                                              | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
91: | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
92: | Reddit threads/comments               | `scrapecreators`                       | Deepline integration API key                                                   | Required for managed Reddit comments/thread coverage.                                                                                                                                                       |
93: | TikTok / Instagram / YouTube fallback | `scrapecreators`                       | Deepline integration API key                                                   | Preferred managed API for captions, engagement, and transcript fallback. Search ScrapeCreators unfiltered when profile/contact tools matter; some profile tools are categorized as `admin`, not `research`. |
94: | X/Twitter                             | `twitterapi`                           | Deepline integration API key                                                   | Managed X/Twitter search; avoids scraping x.com.                                                                                                                                                            |
95: | Web/news/docs                         | `serper`                               | Deepline integration API key or `SERPER_API_KEY` for server-owned dev/prod use | Search API, not search-page scraping.                                                                                                                                                                       |
96: | Web extraction fallback               | `firecrawl` or `exa`                   | Deepline integration API key                                                   | Use after URL discovery; do not use for blind scrape-at-scale.                                                                                                                                              |
97: | Hacker News                           | `hackernews`                           | none                                                                           | Public Algolia API.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
98: | Bluesky                               | `bluesky`                              | none                                                                           | Public AppView API.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
99: | CRM/private                           | Salesforce, HubSpot, Attio             | Deepline OAuth/private connector                                               | Query customer-authorized APIs, not UI scraping.                                                                                                                                                            |
100: | Warehouse/product/workflow            | Snowflake/customer DB/workflow runtime | Deepline private connector                                                     | Use scoped warehouse/runtime access.                                                                                                                                                                        |
101: | Last-resort social actor fallback     | `apify`                                | Deepline integration API key                                                   | Optional fallback only after explicit approval and provider gap status.                                                                                                                                     |
102: 
103: Treat any route not covered by a described Deepline tool contract, key/auth plan, test endpoint, and Deepline-facing pricing as unapproved until after the public research synthesis is complete.
104: 
105: ### 3. Run Public-Source Fanout First
106: 
107: Before provider routing, run a `last30days`-style public discovery pass. The goal is to produce the research synthesis first: what public evidence, communities, registries, directories, reviews, posts, docs, and datasets actually teach us about the GTM problem.
108: 
109: Search across:
110: 
111: - community/social: Reddit threads/comments, X/Twitter, LinkedIn posts if available, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, HN, Bluesky, Polymarket when relevant
112: - web/source discovery: news, blogs, docs, review sites, directories, associations, forums, GitHub, public data inventories
113: - public records and niche datasets: registries, licenses, inspections, permits, government datasets, open CSVs/APIs, professional directories, accreditation/member lists
114: - market-language sources: reviews, comments, clinic/business websites, job posts, competitor pages, support/community language
115: 
116: This pass is search-driven, not recall-driven. Issue real queries. For any vertical dataset, run at minimum these query shapes and read the top results before writing the source line:
117: 
118: - `"<vertical> <entity> registry OR bulk data OR dataset download"` — find the authoritative file
119: - `"<dataset name> download"` / `site:data.gov <vertical>` — find the canonical URL and any mirror
120: - `"<dataset name> parser github"` / `"<dataset name> python"` — find an existing parser/repo so you don't reinvent extraction
121: - `"<vertical> NAICS code"` + `BLS QCEW <NAICS>` / Census County Business Patterns — free establishment counts and sizing
122: 
123: For each useful source lead, record:
124: 
125: - why it matters
126: - **exact artifact**: the specific file/endpoint name, canonical URL, mirror, and any open-source parser/repo (not just "the X bulk feed" or "search Google") — see Non-Negotiables and the Artifact Resolution Gate (§4.55)
127: - whether it can become rows
128: - stable join keys such as NPI, CRD, USDOT#, NAICS, domain, address, phone, license id, provider id, LinkedIn URL, or CRM account id
129: - extraction risks and likely false-positive patterns
130: 
131: Do not stop at "Serper can search this." Search tools are routes; the deliverable is the public source or dataset discovered through them. If you find yourself writing a dataset name you did not just see in a search result, stop and search for it.
132: 
133: ### 3.5. Use The Deepline Pre-Research API After Public Synthesis
134: 
135: When running inside Deepline or the V2 SDK, use the native planning endpoint only after the public-source fanout has produced a first synthesis and source map. The API is for translating the research into Deepline routes, gaps, approval gates, and cost, not for replacing the research pass:
136: 
137: ```bash
138: curl -s "$DEEPLINE_API_BASE_URL/api/v2/pre-research/plan" \
139:   -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEEPLINE_API_KEY" \
140:   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
141:   -d '{"objective":"best GTM data sources for SMB consumer services companies","depth":"deep"}'
142: ```
143: 
144: Agent validation endpoint:
145: 
146: ```bash
147: curl -s "$DEEPLINE_API_BASE_URL/api/v2/pre-research/test" \
148:   -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEEPLINE_API_KEY"
149: ```
150: 
151: The endpoint returns the query plan, source coverage, current Deepline tool candidates, sanitized Deepline-facing pricing metadata, explicit provider gaps, and approval gate. It does not execute paid provider calls.
152: 
153: For SDK V2 users, ask the installed Deepline GTM skill to build the source plan:
154: 
155: ```text
156: /deepline-gtm Build a pre-research source plan for my GTM problem before running paid provider calls.
157: ```
158: 
159: The skill prompts the agent to call `/api/v2/pre-research/plan`, inspect the returned `providerRequirements`, and only then decide whether to run probes or build a play.
160: 
161: ### 4. Search For Deepline Candidate Tools
162: 
163: Run several focused searches, usually in parallel. `deepline tools search` accepts an optional intent query, but requires either that query or one of `--categories` / `--search_terms`; those filters accept comma-separated values. Use `--json` for machine-readable output. There is no `--prefix` flag, so put a provider name in the query instead.
164: 
165: ```bash
166: deepline tools search "web search news source discovery" --categories research --search_terms "web search,news,recency,source discovery"
167: deepline tools search "social posts reddit x twitter youtube tiktok instagram" --categories research --search_terms "social posts,reddit,x twitter,youtube,tiktok,instagram"
168: deepline tools search scrapecreators --json
169: deepline tools search "facebook profile email scrapecreators" --json
170: deepline tools search "instagram profile bio links scrapecreators" --json
171: deepline tools search "company dataset firmographics funding technographics jobs" --categories company_search --search_terms "company dataset,firmographics,funding,technographics,jobs"
172: deepline tools search "crm warehouse workflow session usage" --categories admin --search_terms "crm,warehouse,workflow,session,usage"
173: ```
174: 
175: For CRM/private data, also search by provider name when relevant:
176: 
177: ```bash
178: deepline tools search salesforce
179: deepline tools search hubspot
180: deepline tools search attio
181: deepline tools search snowflake
182: ```
183: 
184: ### 4.25. Design Queries Before Running Tools
185: 
186: Do not send the raw user prompt to every provider. Generate a source-specific query plan first:
187: 
188: ```bash
189: for dir in \
190:   "$PWD/.skills/deepline-pre-research" \
191:   "$HOME/.claude/skills/deepline-pre-research" \
192:   "$HOME/.agents/skills/deepline-pre-research"; do
193:   [ -f "$dir/scripts/query_design.py" ] && SKILL_ROOT="$dir" && break
194: done
195: [ -n "${SKILL_ROOT:-}" ] || { echo "Could not find deepline-pre-research skill root" >&2; exit 1; }
196: python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/query_design.py" "$OBJECTIVE" --depth default
197: ```
198: 
199: Use the plan to decide:
200: 
201: - query type and source tiers
202: - cleaned core subject
203: - Reddit global/review/problem variants
204: - X literal keyword, compound-term, shorter-keyword, and strongest-token fallbacks
205: - video/transcript and caption queries
206: - web, dataset, and GitHub discovery queries
207: - CRM, warehouse, workflow, support, and custom-language private queries
208: - supplemental keys to extract after phase-one retrieval
209: 
210: For production Deepline implementation, port this helper to the runtime language or call equivalent logic before `deepline tools execute`/`deepline enrich`.
211: 
212: ### 4.5. Required Coverage Gate
213: 
214: Before recommending a plan, check every required source family in `references/source-map.md`:
215: 
216: - community/social discussion
217: - custom language and messaging evidence
218: - web/news/search and URL extraction
219: - video/transcript sources
220: - prediction/market/community ranking sources
221: - dataset-discovery leads from social/community results
222: - company/account datasets
223: - person/contact datasets
224: - jobs/hiring/technographic/funding signals
225: - CRM/private datasets
226: - warehouse/product/workflow datasets
227: 
228: For each family, mark one of:
229: 
230: - `native`: a Deepline tool/play exists and can be described
231: - `generic route`: use `apify`, `serper`, `exa`, `parallel`, `firecrawl`, or `deeplineagent`
232: - `private connector`: use CRM, warehouse, workflow, or customer dataset access
233: - `gap`: provider/action should be added before Deepline can replicate that part well
234: 
235: Do not skip a family just because it is inconvenient. Missing coverage is part of the pre-research output.
236: 
237: ### 4.55. Artifact Resolution Gate
238: 
239: Before writing the report, verify every materializable public dataset has been resolved from a _family_ to an _artifact_. For each recommended public dataset/registry, confirm you can fill this row from something you actually searched or fetched this session:
240: 
241: | Dataset | Exact file/endpoint | Canonical URL | Easier mirror | OSS parser/repo | Vertical stat registry (NAICS/QCEW/CBP) |
242: | ------- | ------------------- | ------------- | ------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
243: 
244: Rules:
245: 
246: - A cell you filled from memory instead of a live result is not verified. Search for it.
247: - `n/a` is allowed only when the artifact genuinely does not exist (e.g. no public bulk file, no known parser) — and you must have searched to establish that, not assumed it.
248: - If the user's ask contains "dataset", "github", "repo", "download", "the file", "the data", or a request to hand something over, this gate is the primary deliverable, not an appendix: lead the report with the resolved artifacts.
249: - The government statistical registry column (BLS QCEW + NAICS, Census County Business Patterns) is required for any US industry vertical — it is free establishment-count and sizing data that public-source fanout consistently leaves on the table.
250: 
251: A report that names "the SEC ADV bulk feed" fails this gate; a report that names `IA_FIRM_SEC_Feed_YYYY_MM_DD.xml.gz` at its sec.gov URL, notes the data.gov mirror, and links an existing ADV parser repo passes it.
252: 
253: When you cite a parser/repo alongside a dataset, name the **exact input file that repo actually consumes** — check its README. A vertical often has multiple real distributions (e.g. SEC publishes both the `IA_FIRM_SEC_Feed_*.xml.gz` bulk feed and the `ia<MMDDYY>.zip` IAPD compilation); pairing a parser with the wrong-but-real file is a precision error, not a fabrication, but it still breaks the handoff. Match the parser to its file.
254: 
255: ### 4.6. Fanout And Consolidation Gate
256: 
257: For `last30days` parity, preserve the public-source fanout mechanics described in `references/fanout-consolidation.md`:
258: 
259: - broad parallel search before synthesis
260: - supplemental searches from discovered handles, subreddits, domains, datasets, CRM ids, account lists, workflow ids, and persona language
261: - common evidence rows before scoring
262: - relevance, recency, engagement, source-quality, materializability, private-outcome, join-confidence, custom-language, and cost/coverage scoring
263: - URL/source-id/text dedupe plus company/person/dataset identity joins
264: - coverage nudges for searched, weak, errored, missing-credential, unavailable, and not-relevant sources
265: 
266: If implementation coverage is being audited, run the local evaluator:
267: 
268: ```bash
269: for dir in \
270:   "$PWD/.skills/deepline-pre-research" \
271:   "$HOME/.claude/skills/deepline-pre-research" \
272:   "$HOME/.agents/skills/deepline-pre-research"; do
273:   [ -f "$dir/scripts/evaluate_examples.py" ] && SKILL_ROOT="$dir" && break
274: done
275: [ -n "${SKILL_ROOT:-}" ] || { echo "Could not find deepline-pre-research skill root" >&2; exit 1; }
276: python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/evaluate_examples.py"
277: ```
278: 
279: Use `evals/side-by-side.md` to compare saved `last30days` examples against this skill's coverage contract.
280: 
281: For standalone eval harness runs, write reports into the harness output directory:
282: 
283: ```bash
284: python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/evaluate_examples.py" \
285:   --out-md "${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SKILL_ROOT/evals}/side_by_side_pre_research.md" \
286:   --out-json "${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SKILL_ROOT/evals}/side_by_side_pre_research.json"
287: python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/evaluate_public_private_corpus.py" \
288:   --out-md "${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SKILL_ROOT/evals}/public_private_corpus_results.md" \
289:   --out-json "${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SKILL_ROOT/evals}/public_private_"}}
